name: Northern Salawati
confidence_why: Arnold 2025, the only first-hand description of Northern Salawati, states that the language has no contrastive stress and that stress is predictably word-final, and her 2024 comparative dataset codes every tonal Butlih and Tepin form as final-stressed; the only dissent is her own preliminary 2021 conference slides, which floated lexical stress for Butlih on pairs like [ˈawe] 'child' vs [əˈle] 'cave' before the published analysis reanalysed such words as sesquisyllabic.

catalog_quote: 5.1 SYNCHRONY. The Northern Salawati dialects, like the Maˈya dialects, have two tones—High /³/ and Rise /¹²/—which contrast with toneless syllables. Tonal specification is again largely restricted to word‑final syllables, and toneless words take an optional epenthetic /‑o/ in prepausal position. [...] However, unlike Maˈya, there is no contrastive lexical stress in Northern Salawati; stress is predictably word‑final. In fact, most of the phonetically polysyllabic lexicon of Northern Salawati can be analysed as sesquisyllabic: the nucleus of most non‑final syllables is a non‑stress‑bearing underspecified vowel (represented here as /ə/), the realisation of which is determined by a combination of the vowel of the final syllable and the surrounding consonants. [...] [Table 25, AAM p.36] 1. Contrastive stress — Northern Salawati: N; Batta: N [...] [sec. 5.2.1, AAM p.41] discussed in section 5.1, today all Salawati‑Batta varieties have predictable final stress. [...] [sec. 5.2.4, AAM p.42] However, contrastive stress has been lost in all documented Salawati‑Batta varieties, as they have shifted to a more sesquisyllabic profile.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Salawati (Northern Salawati dialects Butlih, Tepin, Wail) is a tone language (High vs Rise vs toneless, tone confined to the word-final syllable) with no contrastive stress: stress falls predictably on the word-final syllable; non-final syllables mostly carry a reduced, non-stress-bearing underspecified vowel (sesquisyllabic word shape).
new_statements.exceptions: None in Arnold 2025 for Northern Salawati (for sister language Batta, Arnold 2026 says 'with a handful of exceptions'). Arnold's 2021 conference slides had flagged a possible non-final stress in a few Butlih words ([ˈawe] 'child', [ˈmaněn] 'mother' vs [əˈle] 'cave', [məˈnjǎt] 'empty') and a few words with tone on a non-final syllable (/nǎ-lo/ 'sky'); the 2025 peer-reviewed analysis states stress is predictable and final. Underspecified-vowel realisation varies with speech rate (fn.30).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement based on a 324/391-item lexical database, each word recorded 'in a range of different utterance contexts, to accurately determine the word-prosodic specification' (sec. 3); toneless words take optional prepausal epenthetic /-o/. Language is tonal; this is a tonal-with-stress statement (reading fixed: final syllable chosen for the stress rule; alternative label 'tone language with a stress statement').
new_statements.identity_note: Arnold 2025 describes 'Northern Salawati' = the dialect chain across north Salawati island, from first-hand data on three dialects: Butlih (2019), Tepin (2023), Wail (2023); she presumes Fiat, Mucu, Rajau are the same. Kawit (south Salawati; the variety Remijsen 2001:27 equates with the old name 'Maden') has NO prosodic data. Glottolog made1253 'Salawati' [xmx] covers all of these; Batta (Batanta, sister of the Salawati chain, separately described in Arnold 2026 LD&C 20) is a different glottocode and also has predictable final stress. Remijsen's 2001 'Fiawat' wordlist is from a Northern Salawati (Butlih-area) village.

new_statements.quote: I use superscript numerals throughout the worksheets to represent phonological tone. Lower numbers mark lower tone, thus: ¹ (Low tone), ¹² (Rise), ³ (High), ⁴ (Extra-High), and so forth. Stress, which is not predictable in several Maˈya-Salawati varieties and proto-languages, is marked with an accent mark. [...] In As and the Maˈya-Salawati languages, cell colour marks the following specifications: blue = final stress, Extra High tone; green = final stress; High tone, orange = final stress, Rise tone; red = final stress, Low tone; yellow = penultimate stress, High tone (regularly corresponding to penultimate stress, Rise tone in Misool Maˈya); grey = toneless.

new_statements.relation_note: No explicit placement statement, so it cannot 'agree' in words; but the marking convention (accent only where stress is unpredictable; Butlih/Tepin left unmarked, Maˈya marked) and the prosodic key (the Maˈya-Salawati colour classes are all 'final stress' + tone except the yellow penultimate class, which is a Maˈya class) are consistent with the catalog's fixed: final syllable stress and add the detail that the 2025 analysis rests on Butlih + Tepin field data (2019, 2023) with proto-stress inferred from Maˈya. The handful of non-finally accented Butlih items (ˈawe³ 'child', ˈmane¹²n 'mother') are residues of the preliminary 2021 'lexical stress + tone' analysis that Arnold 2025 abandoned.
new_statements.rule_in_words: The dataset contains no prose statement of the Salawati stress rule. It says only that stress is marked with an accent mark where it is 'not predictable' in a variety; the Butlih Salawati (196 forms) and Tepin Salawati (282 forms) columns carry tone superscripts but essentially no stress marks (Butlih: eˈlo³w 'cassowary', ˈawe³ 'child (kin)' flagged 'tonal spec unclear', ˈmane¹²n 'mother', (meˈnin) gowaˈyi³ 'mango'; Tepin: həˈse³lah 'morning'; the other ˈ characters in those columns are gloss quotation marks), whereas Salawati Maˈya (116/244) and proto-Salawati-Batta (122/259) are marked throughout. By the author's own convention this implies that Salawati stress is predictable, consistent with Arnold 2025's 'predictably word-final', but the sheet does not say so in words. The worksheet 'Analysis-OceanicLinguistics' is the calculation sheet behind Arnold 2025 (OL 64) and includes reconstruction notes such as 'Reconstruction inferred from Tepin form; final stress based on Maˈya cognates' — stress in proto-forms is inferred from Maˈya, not from Salawati, again implying Salawati carries no contrastive stress.
new_statements.exceptions: Five Butlih/Tepin forms carry a non-final accent mark (eˈlo³w, ˈawe³ 'tonal spec unclear', ˈmane¹²n with the note 'Irregular Butlih tone; Salawati innovates a (stressed?) *ma- prefix', gowaˈyi³, həˈse³lah); the description's table lists Wail Salawati (wail1246) as a variety but the MASTER sheet has no Wail column (only Butlih, Tepin, Batta under Salawati-Batta).
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog made1253 = ISO xmx 'Salawati' (formerly 'Maden'); Arnold 2020 establishes the name 'Salawati' for the Butlih, Wail, Fiat/Fiawat, Rajau, Tepin, Kawit (and Holo) varieties, which Arnold 2025 groups as 'Northern Salawati' (Butlih, Tepin, Wail documented) within a Salawati-Batta subgroup. Not to be confused with 'Salawati Maˈya' (Glottolog maya1282), the Maˈya dialect spoken on the same island, which does have contrastive stress and is a separate column in the Zenodo dataset. The Zenodo data for xmx are Butlih (field data 2019) and Tepin (field data 2023); Wail is listed in the description but absent from the sheet.

readall_conflicts: Neither newly read work contradicts the catalog. Arnold 2020 (LDD 17) says nothing about stress; the Zenodo 2024 dataset has no prose rule but its conventions (accent marked only where stress is unpredictable; Butlih/Tepin forms unmarked) match Arnold 2025's 'no contrastive lexical stress in Northern Salawati; stress is predictably word-final' (AAM p. 34), which remains the deciding source and the basis of the catalog's fixed: final syllable record. The only tension held by the project is historical: Arnold's 2021 conference slides (already in, not in this task's list) treated Butlih Salawati as 'lexical stress + lexical tone' with [ˈawe] 'child' as a possible non-final stress, and the Zenodo sheet still carries four Butlih and one Tepin form with a non-final accent mark (ˈawe³ flagged 'tonal spec unclear', ˈmane¹²n with a query note about a stressed *ma- prefix). Arnold 2025 supersedes that preliminary analysis by treating non-final vowels as non-stress-bearing underspecified /ə/ in sesquisyllabic words.
